dsc00036-171df22a9e.title: Fifteen minutes in
dsc00036-171df22a9e.body: Fifteen minutes into our first boat tour, and we saw a Harpy Eagle -- the most powerful raptor in the Americas

dsc00108-bbffb10b02.title: White against green
dsc00108-bbffb10b02.body: A snowy egret working the shallows along the Cristalino's clear water.

dsc00408-7339a02d29.title: Standing their ground
dsc00408-7339a02d29.body: A troop of spider monkeys shook branches and barked warnings, trying to scare us off their patch of canopy.

dsc00455-f19d422c73.title: A wary eye
dsc00455-f19d422c73.body: Spider monkeys are thumbless and swing by their tails instead.

dsc00609-6cf622cb46.title: Through the high canopy
dsc00609-6cf622cb46.body: Some of the young spider monkeys had never seen humans before and were more curious than afraid.

dsc01309-90853e40f3.title: The tree fills up
dsc01309-90853e40f3.body: Neotropical cormorants and cattle egrets crowd a single tree at dusk, stacking up branch by branch.

dsc01370-ddb01aff26.title: Golden stare
dsc01370-ddb01aff26.body: Spotting an Amazon milk frog during our night walk.

dsc01461-1d7106395b.title: Coming in for landing
dsc01461-1d7106395b.body: A bee closes in on an Amazon bromeliad - the pink bracts last for weeks, but the blue flowers open for only a day or two.

dsc01907-eb96b3b619.title: Catching fish
dsc01907-eb96b3b619.body: A neotropical otter hauled out on a midstream boulder, grabbing fish with its paws -- we watched it catch seven in a row in the Cristalino river.

dsc02014-2c5f2431c2.title: The taricaya's tears
dsc02014-2c5f2431c2.body: Locals call it the taricaya: a yellow-spotted river turtle basking on a rock while butterflies and bees drink its tears, hunting minerals scarce in the Amazon.

dsc02088-774e6f8bcd.title: Boats at rest
dsc02088-774e6f8bcd.body: Lodge boats resting on the water as the forest went quiet for the night.

dsc02142-e5874bf98c.title: The forest exhales
dsc02142-e5874bf98c.body: Amazon trees release so much water vapor through transpiration that scientists call the resulting moisture flow a 'flying river'

dsc02187-97ac82c963.title: Camouflaged in copper
dsc02187-97ac82c963.body: A night encounter with a Pantanal ocelot, with its chain-like rosettes.

dsc02271-0ee304448c.title: Free ride
dsc02271-0ee304448c.body: A pampas deer doe crossing open grassland with a passenger -- a cattle tyrant riding her back for flushed insects.

dsc02339-de547a705f.title: The Pantanal's emblem
dsc02339-de547a705f.body: A Jabiru stork -- the tallest flying bird in the Americas -- pulling a fresh crab from the grass with its great upturned bill.

dsc02472-c6a4b24f7f.title: Learning the trail
dsc02472-c6a4b24f7f.body: A six-month-old jaguar cub trails close behind its mother - still cautious, still learning.

dsc02518-931c84d465.title: Gardener of the forest
dsc02518-931c84d465.body: South America's largest land mammal - the tapir - browsing in the open at midday. Notoriously shy and difficult to track, this was a rare, clear look at one.

dsc02568-d2b05e28ed.title: An eight-legged crossing
dsc02568-d2b05e28ed.body: A tarantula crossing the track during a safari drive through the Pantanal grounds.

dsc02602-28b6008dba.title: Silhouettes at sunset
dsc02602-28b6008dba.body: A flock of storks cut black against a burning orange Pantanal sunset.

dsc02811-7dfb0b9308.title: Early bird gets the snake
dsc02811-7dfb0b9308.body: Two southern crested caracaras in a tug-of-war over a snake.

dsc02834-b0592de054.title: Ancient and unbothered
dsc02834-b0592de054.body: Hunted hard for its hide in the 1980s, the yacare caiman have since rebounded to some 10 million strong across the Pantanal.

dsc02889-8dc3b09536.title: The cardinal's perch
dsc02889-8dc3b09536.body: A red-crested cardinal atop a flowering tree in the Pantanal.

dsc02921-9e9dd104f6.title: The largest kingfisher alive
dsc02921-9e9dd104f6.body: A ringed kingfisher, the largest kingfisher in the Americas, framed through palm fronds above the water.

dsc03009-4851a7e6ee.title: Jaws ajar
dsc03009-4851a7e6ee.body: Another yacare caiman sunning in the wetland grass, jaws cracked open to cool down.

dsc03028-e5b4bf63ec.title: Waiting for a meal
dsc03028-e5b4bf63ec.body: A trio of lesser yellow-headed vultures waiting on carrion.

dsc03044-342f12324e.title: Beak to beak
dsc03044-342f12324e.body: A bonded pair of the world's largest flying parrot, greeting each other at their nest box.

dsc03126-b2d1854960.title: An armored shuffle
dsc03126-b2d1854960.body: A six-banded armadillo shuffling through the evening grass.

dsc03163-be20f41989.title: Fence Post Sentinel
dsc03163-be20f41989.body: Unlike most owls, burrowing owls hunt by day and nest underground rather than in trees.

dsc03373-d8e19a4866.title: The marsh king
dsc03373-d8e19a4866.body: A marsh deer buck in full antler -- the continent's largest deer, and one of the Pantanal's Big Five alongside the jaguar, tapir and giant anteater.

dsc03598-28bfb8641d.title: Sneaking closer
dsc03598-28bfb8641d.body: A female jaguar approaches, ears back and alert, the male following at a distance.

dsc03604-75617a4a40.title: A few strides closer
dsc03604-75617a4a40.body: The same jaguar, unbothered by the safari jeep, closing the distance step by step.

dsc03644-76be797401.title: The big male, at rest
dsc03644-76be797401.body: The large male settling into the grass -- a rare, close, calm portrait.

dsc03693-aa0fe4ad17.title: Intent on Her
dsc03693-aa0fe4ad17.body: A male jaguar, much larger than his mate, trails after her through the tall grass.

img-0949-7cc238e17d.title: Dwarfed by a tree
img-0949-7cc238e17d.body: A centuries-old Brazil nut tree, one of the giants of the Cristalino.

img-2715-4760f8ea34.title: Golden arches, translated
img-2715-4760f8ea34.body: This São Paulo Mequi - Brazil's nickname for McDonald's - in a converted early-1900s mansion.

img-2723-9b70c4fb57.title: One horizon, endless city
img-2723-9b70c4fb57.body: Walking the skyline on foot, the concrete sea stretching in every direction -- Brazil starts loud.

img-2725-c11d751263.title: The city as canvas
img-2725-c11d751263.body: São Paulo's street-art scene exploded after the city banned outdoor billboards in 2006.

img-2727-a85b9fd07e.title: Churrasco & company
img-2727-a85b9fd07e.body: Dinner at Figueira Rubaiyat -- built around a massive fig tree in the dining room -- with picanha, ribeye, palm heart, and pitu shrimp.

img-2735-28ab2eca22.title: The only way in
img-2735-28ab2eca22.body: Landed at Alta Floresta -- from here, the only way to Cristalino Lodge is by truck, then a transfer onto a boat for the final stretch up the river.

img-2833-dd8abb0b33.title: Right outside our door
img-2833-dd8abb0b33.body: Returning from a hike, we found a capybara grazing a few feet from our room.

img-2842-dcb27a4d93.title: Into the canopy
img-2842-dcb27a4d93.body: Our guide leading the way across the canopy walkway, high above the forest floor.

img-2858-9f914f72cc.title: Sand and clear water
img-2858-9f914f72cc.body: A quiet stretch of white-sand beach on the Cristalino -- shoes off, feet in the warm current.

img-2900-e0815cfa58.title: An unbroken sea of green
img-2900-e0815cfa58.body: Sunrise from the Cristalino Lodge observation deck.

img-2943-daaeb5aadd.title: Wetland gold
img-2943-daaeb5aadd.body: The Pantanal's wetland lagoon glowing gold at sunset -- a quiet close to a wildlife-packed day.

img-2987-03121b254a.title: Copacabana, finally
img-2987-03121b254a.body: The mountains behind, the Atlantic in front -- our first view of Rio from the hotel balcony.

img-3012-8e94da00d6.title: The city lit up gold
img-3012-8e94da00d6.body: Rio's bay and skyline lit gold from the top of Sugarloaf Mountain at sunset.

img-3036-125f159bc3.title: At the feet of Christ the Redeemer
img-3036-125f159bc3.body: The whole family at the base of Christ the Redeemer, high above the city on Corcovado.

img-3048-9ef580c62e.title: Together at the top
img-3048-9ef580c62e.body: The family at the summit platform, Christ the Redeemer towering just behind us.

img-3055-3e5a6402a5.title: Under open arms
img-3055-3e5a6402a5.body: Standing at the base of Christ the Redeemer atop Corcovado

img-3099-fbb79ec833.title: Copacabana Beach
img-3099-fbb79ec833.body: Sunset from the rooftop bar at the Emiliano, our hotel on Copacabana.

por-maycon-nunes-photography-112-971c4c9.title: A crash course in Carnaval
por-maycon-nunes-photography-112-971c4c9.body: Behind the scenes at the warehouse of Grande Rio, one of Rio's top samba schools - costumes, drums, and a quick samba lesson included.

por-maycon-nunes-photography-144-aa3bc0d.title: The Lapa Steps
por-maycon-nunes-photography-144-aa3bc0d.body: 215 steps that the Chilean artist Jorge Selarón tiled by hand from 1990 until his death in 2013, using tiles sent to him from more than 60 countries.

por-maycon-nunes-photography-148-eee1373.title: The Lapa Steps
por-maycon-nunes-photography-148-eee1373.body: 215 steps that the Chilean artist Jorge Selarón tiled by hand from 1990 until his death in 2013, using tiles sent to him from more than 60 countries.

notes.text: this is very similar to the last set of text for the last photo. can you suggest alternatives?

This was the duplicate. Frame 5 (“The Lapa Steps”) already carries Selarón, the 215 steps, 1990–2013 and the 60 countries — your body here repeated all four, so I've let frame 5 keep the history and given this one the moment instead. Also corrected “mid-staircase”: you're on the cobbles at the bottom. The tribute-colours line moved to frame 7, where the green and yellow is actually in shot. Alternatives: “The four of us, bottom of the steps” or “Before the climb”.

por-maycon-nunes-photography-158-5d1c81c.title: Sitting on a Landmark
por-maycon-nunes-photography-158-5d1c81c.body: The green and yellow tiles are Selarón's tribute to Brazil — the country he adopted, and dedicated the staircase to.

notes.text: Kept your title. Moved the red/yellow/green tribute line here from frame 6 because this is the frame where you can actually see it — that flag-coloured wave fills the wall behind them. Alternatives: keep your “more than 2,000 tiles, no two quite match” (it's good, it just also fits frame 5) or “They sat down; everyone else kept climbing”.

Retitled — “Christ the Redeemer” promised a portrait of the statue, but here it's a speck and the real subject is the peak with the four of you under it. Gave this frame the 710m/30m numbers, which is why I took them off frame 11 (they were the only fact that frame had, and the two shots are close enough that repeating them would read as a copy-paste). Alternatives: “The whole mountain in one frame” or “The classic view, from the other side of the valley”.

por-maycon-nunes-photography-247-11de0d9.title: The walk-and-talk
por-maycon-nunes-photography-247-11de0d9.body: Our photographer's favorite trick: keep walking, don't look at the camera. Corcovado handles the rest of the frame.

por-maycon-nunes-photography-27-479a6587.title: Sunburst Costume
por-maycon-nunes-photography-27-479a6587.body: A "fantasia" opening costume — built on a rattan frame so the whole structure rides on one person's shoulders.

notes.text: can you suggest more changes here

Retitled because it isn't a head dress — that radial sunburst is the whole costume and he's inside it. Alternatives: “Ian, inside the whole thing” (warmer) or “One person carries all of this” (leads with the fact).

por-maycon-nunes-photography-283-f34b185.title: Through the branches
por-maycon-nunes-photography-283-f34b185.body: Christ the Redeemer: 710 meters of granite with the 30-meter statue standing on top of it.

notes.text: more options for through the branches?

Kept your title, it earns the shot. The 30m/710m measurements went to frame 8 (the wide view), so this one needed its own fact — the forest doing the framing is hand-planted, which is a better fit for a photo that is mostly leaves. Alternatives: “Corcovado, half hidden” or “The forest gets in the way, pleasantly”.

por-maycon-nunes-photography-293-a3cbf13.title: Backlit at golden hour
por-maycon-nunes-photography-293-a3cbf13.body: The same statue four hours and one mountain later, shot from Morro da Urca as the sun went down behind Corcovado.

por-maycon-nunes-photography-327-4bab5f0.title: The four of us, and the loaf
por-maycon-nunes-photography-327-4bab5f0.body: Portuguese traders called it Pão de Açúcar -- sugarloaf -- after the conical clay molds that refined sugar was shipped in.

por-maycon-nunes-photography-335-1eb3f2b.title: The cable line down
por-maycon-nunes-photography-335-1eb3f2b.body: The final descent from Sugarloaf, Rio's lights beginning to flicker on against the last orange glow over the mountains.

por-maycon-nunes-photography-340-f2f7b79.title: Blue hour crowd
por-maycon-nunes-photography-340-f2f7b79.body: Everyone waiting for the last of the sunset to give way to the city lights.

notes.text: can you suggest more changes here too? don't really like this text

Kept your title. The old body ended on “a lot more weight than it looks”, which is a feeling rather than a thing — swapped it for the football-pitch print and banknote cuffs, which are visible and odd enough to earn the line. Alternatives: “A football pitch, and money at the wrists” or “Every one of these has paraded”.
